$comment: COMCON C2 — the typed schema of the confined tenant ENVIRONMENT. This is the machine-readable type surface a tenant fragment may reference; the typed-profile front-end (C3) type-checks fragments against it, and the lowering (C5) erases against it. It covers only the small REAL tenant surface (deny-by-default: no `nginx`, no COM). The host COM surface — typed from the describe() registry with read-only-getter rows — is a later C2 extension. Grounded: t/comcon_schema_conformance.t proves this matches the running surface.

numeric.$comment: V1 numeric discipline. JS doubles are normative in both tiers (T1/T2). The typed integer is a safe-integer refinement.

int.repr: IEEE-754 double restricted to safe integers

numeric.rule: No host op may expose a numeric domain past the safe-integer range: ms not ns for timestamps, scaled units for large quantities, strings (or opaque handles) for true 64-bit identifiers. Enforced per schema row.

Request.note: Plain request DATA — no capability. A copy; mutating it does nothing.

Response.note: The tenant's ENTIRE authority over the response. Data out, no capability.

key.domain: token chars [A-Za-z0-9_-]; framing/hop-by-hop names rejected (SR-1 MEDIUM-2)

Socket.note: A host-granted capability. Scalar reads are the intended use; reach edges (.listener) and mutators (close/broadcast) are compartment-gated.

Listener.note: Reachable only by the owning compartment; a tenant handed a foreign socket gets null here.

env.$comment: Names bound in EVERY confined tenant fragment (deny-by-default: these and only these, plus host grants).

report.note: The one always-granted capability: write a line to the host log.

onRequest.note: Register the request handler. Its return value IS the response.

grants.$comment: Optional, host-authorized (nginx.grantToTenant). Present only when granted; bound by the name the host chose.

socket.note: A tenant HOLDS the object but the A1 gates bound what it can reach.
